svg.title: B26 / HELIOS POWERLOOP — Solar Electrolysis Dispatch engineering mission profile
svg.desc: B26, HELIOS POWERLOOP — Solar Electrolysis Dispatch. Original project: Electrolytic Application of Load-Managing Photovoltaic System. Session B: Earth & Environmental Engineering. Scientific question: Which dispatch policy balances curtailed solar, hydrogen cost, load service and electrolyzer lifetime across weather and demand uncertainty? Testable hypothesis: A degradation-aware controller may reduce costly cycling with modest loss of immediate hydrogen output; batteries help only where avoided wear/curtailment exceeds their cost and losses.. svg.text: Electrolytic Application of Load-Managing Photovoltaic System
No project observations acquired · specified cases await execution · shared demonstrations are separately labeled
Create a simulation-based design for photovoltaic electricity allocated
among fixed loads, an electrolyzer, storage and curtailment. Optimize useful
hydrogen and grid/load performance while accounting for cycling, degradation
and water. Treat dispatch as a constrained engineering model; no hardware
safety or operating envelope is inferred from an unconstrained optimum.
Which dispatch policy balances curtailed solar, hydrogen cost, load service
and electrolyzer lifetime across weather and demand uncertainty?
TESTABLE HYPOTHESIS / NOT AN OBSERVED RESULT
A degradation-aware controller may reduce costly cycling with modest loss of
immediate hydrogen output; batteries help only where avoided
wear/curtailment exceeds their cost and losses.
Faraday relation does not determine total system efficiency or auxiliary
Minimum load, ramping and start/stop bounds are equipment-specific.
Grid carbon, tariffs and water scarcity vary by place/time.
VALIDITY LIMITS / THE CLAIM STOPS HERE
Generic wear models may not transfer to a particular stack. Tariff/market
access and water availability can dominate economics; simulations cannot
establish hardware readiness or safe operating limits.
COUNTS OF RECORDS · NO COMPLETION SCORES
TRACEABILITY / IDs THAT STAY WITH THE WORK
Execution evidence is required before case closure.
References are pointers; archive acquisition is separate.
A question becomes a model. A model earns evidence.
NASA-inspired mission names are creative identifiers. This profile describes research design; it claims no NASA approval or flight qualification.
Original titles are preserved. Data pointers and citations do not establish that the original teams’ observations have been acquired.
